items.title: James Chirillo interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2007
items.q: You know he said he’d only been playing the guitar for three years when he ended up in that trio. Slam had perfect pitch...

ctx.x: You know he said he’d only been playing the guitar for three years when he ended up in that trio. Slam had perfect pitch so if Art just sort went that-a-way he’d go, but neither of those guys would be telling him nothing. But there was one good one where — Bill Finegan told me this one — that trio was playing somewhere, at some joint. Art Tatum’s doing “Lover” and of course he’s totally tearing it up and it’s [claps], tearing it up for chorus after chorus. Totally tearing it up. So he’s rolling around on this…

Well that’s hard to — I used to play with a guitar player like that who played so much, so much for so many choruses, then he says, “You got it.” So I said you already said all of it. I have nothing to add.
